findings.title: Zoom controls remain enabled while browser interaction is locked
findings.trigger: A login, login import, or active browser turn sets navigationLocked=true, or the browser is hidden; the user activates a zoom control.
findings.actual: Back, Forward, and Reload use navigationLocked and visibility guards, but Zoom out, Reset zoom, and Zoom in do not. Their handler also calls zoomBrowser without the lock guard.
findings.expected: All browser-mutating controls are disabled while the browser surface is locked or unavailable, then re-enabled after the operation ends.
findings.smallestFix: Use navigationLocked || !visible for all zoom controls and keep the same guard in zoom().

findings.title: Browser navigation stays actionable during MCP verification
findings.trigger: MCP Verify runtime is running with operation.name=mcp-verification and no active browser turn; the user activates Back, Forward, or Reload.
findings.actual: unrelatedOperation is computed but omitted from navigationLocked, so navigate() and the three navigation buttons remain active during verification.
findings.expected: Navigation is disabled for the duration of browser-owned connector verification and restored after completion or failure.
findings.smallestFix: Include running mcp-verification and equivalent browser-inspection operations in navigationLocked and retain the navigate() guard.

findings.title: Expanded MCP tutorial is modal without focus trapping or focus restoration
findings.trigger: The user opens the expanded MCP tutorial video and tabs or closes it with Escape/Close.
findings.actual: The portal declares role=dialog and aria-modal=true and autofocuses Close, but Tab can leave the dialog and closing does not restore focus to the expand control.
findings.expected: Focus stays inside the modal and returns to the opener on close.
findings.smallestFix: Add a small focus trap, retain an opener ref, and restore focus from closeExpanded().

findings.title: ARIA tabs contain nested close buttons with conflicting keyboard behavior
findings.trigger: A keyboard user navigates the tablist and reaches a closable tab’s close button.
findings.actual: Each role=tab is a clickable div containing a native button; the tab handler ignores key events from the nested button, so the roving tab behavior and close-control focus model diverge.
findings.expected: The tablist has one coherent roving-focus model, with a separately exposed and intentionally managed close action.
findings.smallestFix: Implement explicit tab/close focus handling or a documented tablist pattern, add aria-controls, and keep the close action separately labelled.
